Encounter budgets and CV calibration

Agreed targets: four player characters are the reference party; typical combat about 4 rounds, hard about 6, extreme about 10. Typical reasonably prepared parties should have roughly a 20–30% chance of at least one new wound without a healer, 5–15% with one. These are feel targets, not mandatory outcomes for every battle.

Proposed budget procedure

Define B(L) as the calibrated standard encounter budget for four characters of level L. For N characters of the same level:

Budget = B(L) × N / 4 × difficulty multiplier.

Proposed multipliers: easy 0.75, standard 1.00, hard 1.50, extreme 2.00. Round the final budget to a convenient whole CV. These multipliers are starting fixtures, not verified mappings to encounter duration. An extreme encounter must not simply be declared a ten-round fight because its budget doubled.

For mixed levels, use sum(B(character level) / 4), then multiply by difficulty. This preserves each character’s calibrated contribution rather than rounding the party’s average level. Budget is the sum of participating enemies’ CV. Waves and reinforcements count; terrain and mission objectives require separate review.

Arithmetic example only: if future calibration establishes B(1)=40, three level-1 characters receive a standard budget of 30; five receive 50. A hard fight for five would be 75. Forty is a demonstration input, not an assigned level-1 budget.

Proposed creature estimate, followed by testing

Start with CV estimate = sqrt(E × O) × U, normalized so a chosen reference creature has the desired reference CV.

- E = expected attacks needed to defeat it using the reference party’s actual attack outcomes, hit effects, resistances and relevant control. Do not divide HP by a single raw damage number that ignores minimum damage. - O = expected effective HP damage per round against that party, counting actual targets, action economy and healing. Use recorded outcome probabilities and attack/defense attributes, not an assumed universal success rate. - U = an explicit provisional adjustment for disabling effects, movement, unusual senses, reach, summoning or other advantages not represented by E and O. Start at 1 for an ordinary damage-only creature; document every other value.

This is a seed metric, not a final algorithm. Zero-damage controllers cannot receive zero CV: evaluate their contribution in a mixed encounter instead of applying this formula blindly. Healing loops, area attacks and incapacitation can make the simple estimate unreliable. Record uncertainty rather than publishing false precision.

Calibration sequence for the bestiary

1. Build a few ordinary melee/ranged creatures with full printed attack and defense attributes, HP, resistances, Stability, actions and outcomes. 2. Test actual level-1 parties with documented supplies and healing access. 3. Fit B(1) and creature CV to duration, wound incidence, defeat risk and action loss. 4. Test 3-, 4- and 5-character parties and easy/hard/extreme multipliers. Include open and obstructed terrain; party-size scaling may need an enemy-count warning. 5. Add control, healing and summons one feature at a time; refine U or replace the seed metric if it fails. Then repeat at levels 3 and 7 and intermediate levels.

Until those tests exist, CV and B(L) remain uncalibrated. The procedure is ready to support bestiary development; numerical encounter guarantees are not.

Bestiary seed worksheet

The bestiary encounter draft now supplies explicit reference attacks, enumerated probabilities, utility factors and a proposed B(L)=32+8L testing grid. These are authoring seeds, not the completed calibration described above. Every creature’s CV can be recomputed by the bestiary audit.
